executiveSummary: GM0147 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, population, 15 neighbourhoods, Borne/Hertme/Zenderen place membership, settlement labels, Borne station and six NWB-derived links are coherent; official nulls, zero-intensity behavior, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, cumulative event-attributable service-pressure person-hours and map-layer invariance also pass. Release remains correction-required for two reproducible spatial contradictions. First, a three-line Rhine/Meuse/IJssel proximity screen assigns Borne a municipality-wide normalized inundation-stress amplitude of 0.466645 at both T+24 and T+72, although the current Twente risk profile describes primarily local, short-lived brook/rain effects and no selected connected hydraulic scenario supports that direct major-river field. Second, a focused T+24 ignition inside an official TOP10NL broadleaf-forest polygon in BU01470009 makes that source neighbourhood rank only eleventh, because all neighbourhood hazards are allocated with one source-insensitive hash. The same order is reused for river, pluvial and heat; Wensink-Zuid happens to rank first, but the model does not use Borne's documented south-to-north gravity sewer, buffers, blue artery, retention or climate-stress maps. Public context is useful but non-causal: the current boundary snapshot intersects 82 water-board objects, one station, 125 transit-stop records, 42 antenna registrations, three government-service records, 13 education records and no matching RIVM acute-care record. Zero acute-care records and an empty drainage-provider response are not zero care or zero drainage. Physical Enexis, Coteq, Vitens, sewer, telecom, facility and supply topology, live state, backups, stocks, crews and restoration commitments remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented; all eight service views correctly call their shared A1/A35/N743/N744 flows logical transfer proxies.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 — filtered rows for GM0147
supports: Official-context GM0147/Borne identity, population 24,741, density 952 residents per square kilometre, age-65-plus count 5,713 and 3,006 one-person households.

The machine-readable OData table is an annual official statistical release under CC BY 4.0; independently rounded neighbourhood rows require reconciliation and suppressed, unknown or not-applicable values must remain null rather than zero.
CBS aggregates are allocation and vulnerability context, not individuals, daytime population, patients, visitors, household preparedness or observed emergency demand.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail
evidenceSources.title: Gemeente and buurt gegeneraliseerd 2025 with BAG, BRT TOP10NL, NWB and railway context
supports: Official annual CC BY 4.0 GM0147 municipality and 15-neighbourhood geometry consumed by the application; the generated reference point and the Borne, Hertme and Zenderen place centres are inside the generalized polygon.

BRT contributes three woonkern labels and TOP10NL supplies national 1:10,000 editioned topography under CC BY 4.0. Broadleaf-forest object 131932696, source date 1 January 2022 and registration date 1 April 2023, contains diagnostic point [6.719467569482939, 52.30339366660814] in BU01470009; static cover is not live fuel moisture, fire spread or an incident perimeter.

NWB is national monthly CC0 road geometry; the generated A1, A35, N743 and N744 crossings are logical scenario corridors, not measured utility routes or evacuation throughput. ProRail station context identifies Borne station but does not establish train availability, passenger capacity or disruption state.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Twente 2025
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 profile, adopted by the general board 23 April 2026
supports: Borne, Hertme and Zenderen sit near Almelo and Hengelo; the built environment is crossed by hazardous-goods rail and lies by the A1/A35, with the Buren–Azelo road stretch highlighted for relatively high accident occurrence.

Twente has relatively high sandy terrain, no primary dike-ring context, and limited river-flood risk dominated by local and generally short-lived effects of prolonged or intense rain around the Regge, Dinkel and smaller waters; indirect consequences from a wider IJssel flood are a separate concern.

The profile identifies drought, limited surface water, nature-fire fuel/access/escape/firewater constraints, storm, winter weather, power, gas, drinking water, wastewater, telecom/ICT and cyber cascades. It distinguishes outage phases from 0–2, 2–8, beyond 8 and beyond 24 hours, supporting a 72-hour exercise horizon without calibrating exact GM0147 values.

It describes induced-earthquake probability in Twente as very small and salt-cavern concerns primarily around Hengelo and Enschede. The strategic profile is scenario/expert context, not a live warning, local incident footprint, probability raster, asset inventory or restoration promise; no machine API or explicit redistribution licence accompanies the PDF.

evidenceSources.title: Informatie over water en riolering and Klimaatadaptief Wensink-Zuid
evidenceSources.edition: live municipal pages and Watertakenplan 2022–2026, inspected 2 September 2026
supports: Borne reports repeated intense-rain impacts and identifies Wensink-Zuid as strategic because the core's gravity sewer slopes from the south through the centre and several residential areas toward the north at 't Dijkhuis.

Published interventions include the Europastraat clean-water line, Van Bemmelstraat underground buffer, a blue artery beneath the F35 rail cycleway, a retention pond, disconnected paved area and the Wensink green/blue public-space system.

The companion page https://www.borne.nl/klimaatadaptief-wensink-zuid says rain regularly causes nuisance/flooding and phases the remaining reconstruction through 2027–2030, explicitly depending on Coteq, Enexis and Vitens work in the subsurface.

These event-updated pages and the downloadable plan are authoritative local engineering/context evidence but do not publish a complete machine-readable sewer graph, live capacity/state, fixed update cadence or explicit data reuse licence.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatatlas Twente and KEA_DATA ArcGIS MapServer
evidenceSources.edition: current regional climate-stress atlas; six-year analysis cycle
supports: The atlas provides local/parcel-scale modeled context for water nuisance, heat, drought and flooding, generally looking toward 2050. Its owner states that it is a stress-test aid rather than an observation or prediction and that the atlas is renewed every six years.

The machine service https://opengeo.wrij.nl/arcgis/rest/services/Klimaat/KEA_DATA/MapServer exposes Twente short-duration T100 and T1000 and long-duration T1000 water-depth rasters plus affected-building and road-passability layers 263–269 in EPSG:28992 with Map, Query and Data access.

At the GM0147 reference point, raster identify returned Pixel Value NoData for layers 263–265; nearby road-passability features did return categorized records. NoData is coverage/response semantics and must not be converted to zero depth or safety.

The atlas warns that worst-case short-rainfall products omit sewer behavior while other municipal stress products may include it. The service metadata inspected did not state native pixel size or a reuse licence, so resolution and redistribution rights must be cleared before caching or causal use.

evidenceSources.publisher: Provincie Overijssel with water boards, Rijkswaterstaat, Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management and Deltares
evidenceSources.title: Updated Overijssel flood-hazard maps under the EU Floods Directive
evidenceSources.edition: public update December 2025; next ROR publication planned 2031
supports: Approximately 80% of scenarios were renewed and smaller brooks and unembanked waters were added where possible; the province says underlying organizations continue updating data while the public ROR reporting cycle is six years.

The machine WMS/WFS capabilities at https://ldo-geoserver.lizard.net/geoserver/ows?service=WMS&version=1.3.0&request=GetCapabilities expose scenario layers that can screen connected flood footprints, but layer-specific resolution, valid scenario, edition and no-data must be pinned.

The catalogue metadata inspected does not establish an ingest-ready blanket licence for every flood layer, so reuse and caching rights require clearance. The provincial B35 watercourse WFS https://services.geodataoverijssel.nl/geoserver/B35_waterlopen/wfs and B32 water-barrier WFS are CC0 and current object context, but line presence alone is not water depth, arrival, duration or failure probability.
The maps are official hazard/scenario context, not an observed current flood or a justification for applying one municipality-wide scalar.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards and Stichting RIONED via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA, Waterketen DAMO and Stedelijk Water GWSW OGC APIs
supports: The current generalized-boundary intersection contains 82 public-context objects: Rioolgemaal Hertme 08004, Rioolgemaal Borne 08001, Rioolgemaal Zenderen 08002 and 79 weirs. Function and capacity are absent in the deployed snapshot and all records are affectsSimulation=false.

Kunstwerken IMWA and companion Waterketen DAMO at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are national OGC services under CC BY-SA 4.0; Kunstwerken declares weekly publication while DAMO cadence and contributor completeness vary.

Stichting RIONED's GWSW OGC/ATOM service https://api.pdok.nl/rioned/beheer-stedelijk-watersystemen-gwsw/ogc/v1 is CC0 with source-managed/unknown cadence and opt-in municipal coverage. The Borne-area query exposes partial water-board wastewater context, including four pumps and a named Saasveld–Hertme–Borne connection, but no complete Borne municipal urban sewer dataset.

Object presence does not establish hydraulic connectivity, catchment, flow direction, capacity, control logic, current operation, emergency power or first-72-hour performance; missing contributors or attributes remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: Netbeheergebieden elektriciteit, gas, media, riolering, warmte en water
evidenceSources.edition: catalogue updated 14 August 2026; provider feature timestamps vary
supports: Public-domain national WMS/WFS at https://public.geodata.mijnaansluiting.nl/geoserver/mijnaansluiting_open/ows identifies providers offering new connections. At the GM0147 reference point the current result is Enexis for electricity, Coteq for gas, Vitens for water and Ziggo for media, with feature lastUpdated 7 September 2025.
Provider polygons are responsibility context, never physical topology, connectivity, capacity, pressure/voltage/coverage quality, telemetry, outage or restoration state.

The drainage query returns no provider because the public sewer layer is contributor-incomplete and historically contains only Waternet participation; it is Unknown coverage, not evidence that Borne has no sewer or drainage service.

Catalogue metadata is event/provider updated rather than a guaranteed operational cadence; feature and retrieval timestamps must be retained and currentness must not be inferred from the catalogue page alone.

identity.summary: GM0147, Borne, Overijssel and safety region Twente are internally and officially coherent.
notes: Generated municipality code/name and feature identity equal GM0147/Borne.
The safety-region layer assigns GM0147 to exactly one region, Twente, and E03 is the current formally adopted regional profile.
No identity, province, boundary/statistics edition or safety-region mismatch was found.

geography.summary: The consumed 2025 generalized boundary and reference point are coherent, while administrative, catchment, sewer, forest and incident geographies remain distinct.
notes: Generated point [6.745700621586728, 52.30860788665645] is inside the official generalized GM0147 polygon; boundaryEdition and statisticsEdition both equal 2025.
E04–E07 distinguish gravity sewer, local storage, small waters, flood scenarios and forest objects from the municipality polygon and its centre.
An administrative neighbourhood, BAG place, BRT label, provider territory, stress-test pixel, sewer catchment, forest polygon and incident footprint are not treated as interchangeable evidence.

demography.summary: Headline municipality statistics match CBS 2025 and independently rounded neighbourhood population reconciles within publication precision.
notes: Generated population 24,741, density 952, age65Pct 23.1 and one-person-household count 3,006 agree with the official municipality record after documented rounding.
The 15 neighbourhood rows sum to 24,735 residents, six below the municipality row (-0.024%); households sum to 10,345 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 5,705.
The simulator proportionally reconciles neighbourhood allocation to exactly 24,741 rather than presenting the independently rounded rows as exact additive counts.
Aggregate age, household, housing, car and access context is not an individual vulnerability record, daytime exposure, medically dependent population or observed emergency demand.

regionalDetail.summary: Fifteen neighbourhoods expose broad aggregate context, but two wholly unavailable fields and administrative averaging constrain operational interpretation.
notes: Population, ages, households, housing, social assistance, businesses, cars, doctor/supermarket distance, land/water, urbanity and address density are populated for all 15 neighbourhoods.

District-heating percentage and public-charging-point count are available in 0/15 neighbourhoods and correctly remain null; they are not converted to zero district heat or zero charging infrastructure.
Largest published neighbourhoods are Bornsche Maten 4,825, Stroom-Esch 3,520, Borne Centrum 3,235, Letterveld II 2,915 and 't Wensink Zuid 2,020 residents.
Compound T+24 local population, affected population and every service demand/delivery total reconcile exactly to the municipality frame.

settlements.summary: Borne, Hertme and Zenderen place and woonkern context remains distinct from the 15 official CBS neighbourhoods.
notes: The three BAG places and three BRT woonkern records are Borne, Hertme and Zenderen; all place centres fall within the generalized municipal boundary.
No out-of-boundary, identity or duplicate-settlement review flag was produced.
Place and settlement labels are not population totals, emergency-facility records, hazard footprints or service nodes.

transport.summary: Six NWB-derived cross-boundary records and Borne station are structurally coherent, but current road/rail performance and service-specific capacity are not observed.
notes: Generated links are A1 and A35 to Almelo, A1 and A35 to Hengelo, N743 to Almelo and N744 to Tubbergen; endpoint fragments total 6.681 km and nominal logical capacity totals 1,340.
ProRail station Borne and 125 GTFS stop records are static infrastructure/schedule context, not proof of operating trains/buses, passenger capacity or first-72-hour availability.

E03's hazardous-goods railway and A1/A35 Buren–Azelo road-risk context is absent from the solver. No timestamped NDW closure, speed, congestion, incident, road passability, evacuation throughput, repair access or rolling-stock state drives the run.
The duplicate A1/A35 neighbor pairs are distinct named road crossings but every service reuses them as nonphysical logical transfer proxies.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong public water, climate, transport, provider and facility context exists, but operational topology/state and validated local capacity are absent.
notes: Official strategic, stress-test, engineering and provider evidence is kept separate from the canonical synthetic scenario clock; none is presented as a T+0 observation or T+72 forecast.

The current boundary snapshot contains 82 HWH water objects, 42 RDI antenna registrations, three KVK government-service records, 13 DUO education records and no RIVM acute-care record. All are display-only/affectsSimulation=false; zero RIVM intersection means no matching surveyed acute-care location, not no health care, patients or demand.

Provider lookup identifies Enexis, Coteq, Vitens and Ziggo at the municipal reference point, while drainage is empty because that layer is incomplete. A point lookup does not prove full-boundary coverage, and no result is Unknown rather than zero service.

No authorized feeder, pipe, pressure zone, complete sewer catchment, antenna backhaul/coverage, facility continuity, pharmacy/food/fuel stock, priority-customer, crew or restoration dataset is loaded or inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at all six required checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Peak municipality severities were storm 0.615672, pluvial 0.415290, river 0.144940, coastal 0, heat 0.648229, winter 0.563801, cyber 0.432891, earthquake 0.083274, wildfire 0.104728 and compound 0.871602.

At T+24 compound had rain 46.509509 mm/h, normalized inundation-stress amplitude 0.383600, wind 26.860191 m/s, cyber disruption 0.379774, severity 0.856649, system pressure 0.487512, 12,113 modeled people under pressure and 219,860 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours.

At T+72 compound retained normalized inundation-stress amplitude 0.383600 and cyber disruption 0.049394, with severity 0.419540, pressure 0.517205, 13,149 modeled people under pressure and 880,858 cumulative proxy person-hours.

Canonical coastal direct inundation and headline severity remain zero in Borne while its modeled wind tail still produces service pressure; this must be read as indirect storm/service scenario effect, not coastal flooding. Canonical wildfire is transported smoke/drought with zero direct flame; the focused forest ignition is a separate reproducibility test.

The remote Groningen-centered earthquake, generic untargeted cyber run and all meteorological values are deterministic exercise assumptions, not observations, probabilities, warnings, attack intelligence or outage forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, cumulative burden, route bounds, local reconciliation and layer invariance pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0147 pnpm audit:model passed both focused coverage tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 29.68 seconds (29.49 seconds test execution) on the final rerun.
Every preset at intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every required checkpoint.

Repeated frames are deterministic; outputs are finite and bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity; all eight headline pressure weights participate and close to one.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciles population 24,741, affected population 12,113 and all eight demand/delivery balances, with maximum observed floating-point discrepancy 3.55e-15.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The major-river proximity screen and source-insensitive neighbourhood allocator contradict Borne's public hydraulic and forest evidence.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-467 derives Rhine/Meuse/IJssel exposure only from municipality-reference-point distance to three approximate line segments; GM0147 is inside its 50 km support although no selected connected defence, breach, depth, arrival, duration or recession surface is supplied.

At T+24 and T+72 the river preset retains normalized inundation-stress amplitude 0.466645 and severity 0.144940; modeled people under pressure are 3,474 then 4,377 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours are 71,678 then 297,733.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3480-3494 applies the same seeded regional multiplier to municipality severity. River, pluvial and heat therefore have the identical top-five order: 't Wensink Zuid, Borne Centrum, Zenderen, Verspreide huizen Hertme and Tichelkamp.

E04 supports Wensink-Zuid and downstream core sensitivity, but the matching rank is coincidental: no gravity sewer, clean-water pipe, buffer, retention, catchment, stress-test raster or NoData mask determines it.

A focused synthetic T+24 source [6.719467569482939, 52.30339366660814] intersects official TOP10NL broadleaf forest and BU01470009. Direct fire is 0.503952 and municipality severity 0.481791, but the source neighbourhood ranks eleventh at 0.423796 while 't Wensink Zuid ranks first at 0.538143.
River and wildfire emit derived-screening/synthetic evidence rather than source-supported local footprints, so they must not support neighbourhood dispatch, evacuation or resource-priority claims.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances and dependency stages are inspectable, but magnitudes are not calibrated to Borne's providers, water system, facilities, rail/road access or supply chain.
notes: Compound T+24 availability was power 0.177386, water 0.619406, drainage 0.400608, gas 0.714180, telecom 0.583683, mobility 0.223261, facilities 0.746428 and supply 0.749913.

E03 supports the direction and timing importance of electricity, telecom, water, wastewater, mobility, facility and supply cascades; E04/E07 establish local drainage architecture and registered assets. None calibrates the exact availability, demand, delivery, reserve, backup or repair values.

The graph has no named Borne/Hertme/Zenderen pump/catchment chain, Wensink gravity path, blue artery/storage state, Enexis feeder, Coteq gas zone, Vitens pressure area, Ziggo/backhaul path, station continuity, health-care role or food/fuel depot.
All eight service views reuse the same six A1/A35/N743/N744 NWB-derived routes and total nominal capacity 1,340; emitted transferSemantics remains logical-proxy rather than physical utility topology.

Aggregate household, housing, business, car and distance context changes local demand transparently, but coefficients remain scenario assumptions rather than individual vulnerability or measured first-72-hour demand.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve confidence, dependency order, scenario operations and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; every service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service shortfalls sum to municipality pressure.
Dependency chains, local context factors, drivers, recovery progress and restore-service counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Day type, local start clock, demand, backup, network and repair multipliers are normalized and labeled scenario operations assumptions; delayed interventions do not masquerade as known crews/assets.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure against a matched no-event baseline; they are not observed outage-hours, casualties, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water repair gating behaves consistently, but no selected local event, asset, access, backup or crew evidence calibrates Borne restoration through T+72.
notes: For river flooding, normalized inundation stress remains 0.466645 through T+72 and recoveryProgress remains exactly zero for all eight services; power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/supply availabilities remain 0.937566/0.740080/0.860505/0.767609/0.483658/0.916994/0.528225 while facilities falls from 0.793973 to 0.609048 through dependency dynamics.

For compound, inundation stress remains 0.383600 and recoveryProgress is zero for every service at T+72; power remains limiting at 0.162364 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours reach 880,858.
This verifies the sustained-active-water recovery guard. It does not validate the unsupported major-river premise, exact persistence or a claim that all local systems receive no repair for 72 hours.

Storm, pluvial, winter, wildfire and earthquake envelopes numerically recede by T+72; heat retains drought within its long canonical event and cyber retains 0.043289 severity. None is calibrated to a dated Borne incident.
No public source supplies event-specific damage, live operating state, generator/fuel endurance, priority customers, staff, stocks, repair access, crews, mutual aid or restoration commitments.

findings.summary: A coarse named-major-river proximity field presents unsupported persistent direct Borne inundation without a selected connected hydraulic scenario.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-467 uses only municipality-reference-point distance to three approximate Rhine/Meuse/IJssel segments. At T+24 and T+72 the canonical river preset reports normalized inundation-stress amplitude 0.466645, severity 0.144940 and zero recovery across all services; modeled people under pressure are 3,474 then 4,377 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours 71,678 then 297,733. E03 describes Twente as relatively high, outside primary dike-ring context and mainly exposed to limited/local, short-lived effects around smaller waters and extreme rain, while E06 supplies scenario-specific public flood maps. No selected defence, connection, water level, depth, arrival, duration or recession surface supports the displayed direct GM0147 field. This is municipality-specific evidence of a shared 50-km proximity-screen defect, not a claim that Borne is flood-safe or insulated from indirect IJssel effects.
findings.action: Make unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing numerically neutral/Unknown for GM0147 until an expert selects a named, versioned, hydraulically connected ROR/LIWO scenario. Preserve separately labeled local brook, groundwater, pluvial, sewer and indirect supply/transport consequences.

findings.summary: An explicit source inside a Borne broadleaf-forest polygon does not control the neighbourhood map presented as local wildfire impact.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies current TOP10NL broadleaf-forest object 131932696 and diagnostic source [6.719467569482939, 52.30339366660814] inside BU01470009 Verspreide huizen Borne-West. A focused synthetic T+24 run reports direct fire 0.503952, smoke 0.412358, drought 0.471937 and municipality severity 0.481791, yet BU01470009 ranks eleventh at 0.423796 while 't Wensink Zuid ranks first at 0.538143. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:842-887 uses a municipality reference-point circle, and model.ts:3480-3494 never intersects the local source, incident perimeter or eligible fuel. E03 says fuel, wind, access, evacuation routes, scarce surface/firewater and response time matter. This diagnostic is not an observed incident or forecast.
findings.action: Keep direct-fire neighbourhood ranks visibly synthetic/unsupported and prohibit operational rank use. Make local allocation source/perimeter and eligible-fuel aware, while modeling transported smoke, drought, wind, access, extinguishing water and suppression assumptions separately.

findings.summary: Borne's documented gravity-sewer and Wensink storage system is absent; one shared hash makes unrelated river, pluvial and heat neighbourhood maps identical.
findings.evidence: E04 identifies Wensink-Zuid as a recurring rain-nuisance area and the strategic upstream end of a gravity sewer flowing north through central neighborhoods, with named clean-water conveyance, buffer, blue-artery and retention interventions. E05 offers event-specific stress-test surfaces and explicit NoData. Nevertheless model.ts:3480-3494 gives river, pluvial and heat the identical top-five T+24 order: 't Wensink Zuid, Borne Centrum, Zenderen, Verspreide huizen Hertme and Tichelkamp. Wensink-Zuid's pluvial severity is 0.299436, but the plausible top rank is not causal evidence: no terrain pixel, impervious surface, sewer catchment, inlet, pipe, buffer, pump, outlet or downstream water level determines it.
findings.action: Label all local water/heat ranks synthetic pending integration. Use the event/return-period-specific Klimaatatlas layers and a licensed municipal GWSW/stress-test export with units, grid size, edition, no-data, uncertainty and licence retained; never convert NoData to zero or mix 2050 scenario context with live T+0 conditions.

findings.summary: Eighty-two official water-board objects improve context but do not establish Borne drainage connectivity, capacity, state or restoration.
findings.evidence: E07 contributes three named sewer pumps and 79 weirs inside the generalized boundary, while E04 documents municipal pipes, storage and gravity direction. The application correctly marks all 82 objects affectsSimulation=false and their function/capacity fields are absent. Compound T+24/T+72 drainage availability 0.400608/0.386372 arises from generic equations, not catchment connectivity, pipe/pump/weir capacity, inlet blockage, storage, overflow, receiving-water level, controls, emergency power or telemetry. The GWSW query is only partial water-board wastewater context; missing municipal data is Unknown.
findings.action: Keep IMWA/DAMO/GWSW objects as partial non-causal context. Obtain a licensed, security-reviewed municipal sewer/stress-test graph and exercise state before causal use; otherwise expose named bounded subsystem assumptions with connectivity, capacity, backup and state explicitly Unknown.

findings.summary: The same six road corridors are cloned across all eight services and cannot represent Borne's physical utility, facility or supply topology.
findings.evidence: Six NWB-derived crossings totaling nominal logical capacity 1,340 connect GM0147 to Almelo, Hengelo and Tubbergen. The engine applies the same A1/A35/N743/N744 records to power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply. E03/E04/E07/E08 establish discipline-specific providers and dependencies, not shared road topology. The engine/UI correctly emit transferSemantics logical-proxy, but road direction, nominal capacity and flow are not feeders, pipes, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food/fuel routes.
findings.action: Keep logical-proxy language and prevent these flows from supporting physical claims. Restrict NWB/NDW to mobility and repair/supply access; add utility/facility edges only from operator-authorized topology or clearly named editable exercise gateways with capacity and live state Unknown by default.

findings.summary: Borne's station, hazardous-goods railway and A1/A35 incident exposure are visible only as static context and do not drive first-72-hour access or dependencies.
findings.evidence: E02 and the deployed data identify Borne station and 125 GTFS stop records; E03 specifically identifies hazardous-goods rail through built-up areas and relatively high road-accident occurrence on Buren–Azelo. The simulation uses six municipal road endpoint links but no rail corridor consequence, current timetable trip, NDW closure/incident/speed, flooded-road passability, evacuation throughput, response access or repair-route state. Compound mobility availability 0.223261 at T+24 and 0.206343 at T+72 is therefore a scenario balance, not an observed network state.
findings.action: Integrate ProRail/GTFS geometry and service windows as dated context and NDW DATEX II CC0 event-valid traffic/closure data for mobility only, preserving observed timestamp and coverage. Model hazardous-material and rail shutdown as explicitly selected scenarios; do not infer emergency capacity or train continuity from stations/stops.

findings.summary: Provider polygons, antennas, schools and demographic aggregates do not resolve first-72-hour power, gas, water, telecom, care or household continuity.
findings.evidence: E01 supports Borne's relatively older population and 3,006 one-person households; E08 identifies Enexis, Coteq, Vitens and Ziggo responsibility context. The display snapshot intersects 42 RDI antenna registrations, three public-order/safety records, 13 education records and no RIVM acute-care location. None establishes feeder/pipe/backhaul topology, coverage, load, priority customers, backup duration, occupancy, care role, staffing, shelter status or stocks. Compound T+24 power 0.177386, gas 0.714180, water 0.619406, telecom 0.583683, facilities 0.746428 and supply 0.749913 are synthetic scenario balances, not provider/facility observations.
findings.action: Keep provider and public registries display-only with publisher, edition, retrieval time, coverage and licence. Use capacity, state, backup, stock and restoration only from authorized operator/GHOR exercise inputs; otherwise retain the smallest service-specific synthetic prior and explicit Unknown.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake and remote coastal effects are bounded exercises but not locally calibrated Borne forecasts or probabilities.
findings.evidence: E03 establishes that storm, drought, heat, winter weather, utility failures and cyber cascades matter, but calls Twente earthquake chance very small and locates salt-cavern concern mainly near Hengelo/Enschede. The canonical Borne peaks are storm 0.615672, heat 0.648229, winter 0.563801, cyber 0.432891 and remote Groningen-centered earthquake 0.083274. Coastal direct water and headline severity are zero, yet a modeled wind tail yields T+24 pressure 0.153970, 487 people under pressure and 20,378 cumulative person-hours. Untargeted cyber assigns generic exposure and meteorological values are deterministic seasonal equations, not valid-time KNMI observations. These results are scenario consequences conditional on assumptions, not annual likelihood, live weather, attack intelligence or infrastructure outage.
findings.action: Keep scenario/observed/probability labels distinct. Allow source and target selection; add versioned KNMI observed/forecast inputs only with valid time and coverage, and use local underground/cyber effects only through selected expert scenarios or authorized aggregate operator fragility envelopes.

findings.summary: The current data adapter preserves documented null, empty-coverage and display-only semantics instead of silently turning missing evidence into zero or truth.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Borne disaster, outage, casualty, evacuation, welfare or restoration dataset.
The 2025 generalized CBS boundary is suitable for municipal aggregation but not parcel-level hydraulics, asset ownership, response jurisdiction or exact incident geometry.

The public Twente climate atlas is modeled stress-test context; map variants differ in sewer inclusion, the inspected raster can return NoData, and licence/native resolution require clearance before ingestion.
Flood-layer availability does not prove hydraulic connection; an expert must select and version a physically relevant ROR/LIWO scenario before direct Borne inundation is simulated.
TOP10NL forest cover is static topography rather than live fuel, moisture, wind-driven spread, suppression or access state; the focused ignition is synthetic.
HWH/GWSW/provider/antenna/facility/station/GTFS records are partial static context, not complete topology, capacity, operating state, backup, stock or restoration commitments.
No reviewed public safe source provides complete Enexis, Coteq, Vitens, municipal sewer, telecom, care, food/fuel or emergency-resource topology/state; sensitive detail was not inferred.
